expectations.text: The redesign only realizes rows/tiles near the viewport (a window plus small buffer), not the entire catalog at mount
expectations.evidence: realizes only visible +/-2 view window, +/-1 image window

expectations.text: Rows/tiles that scroll far from the viewport are released or recycled (their textures/images freed), so memory plateaus rather than climbing during a long scroll
expectations.evidence: rows leaving window release textures; memory plateaus

expectations.text: The answer distinguishes the full catalog as data from the small window that exists as realized views/textures
expectations.evidence: explicit: full catalog = data, window = views+textures

expectations.text: View recycling / pooling of row or tile nodes is recommended rather than creating and destroying a node per item on every scroll step
expectations.evidence: fixed recycled row-view pool, rebind not create/destroy

expectations.text: The realized window is bounded to roughly one-to-two screens (an explicit small buffer), not an unbounded 'render what's been seen so far'
